question: Why did the error rate go up on 09 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New feature request introduced unexpected load.
why_chain: Feature request R013 for dark mode was submitted 287 minutes before the error rate spike.
The feature request likely caused a temporary increase in load on the service.
This increase in load led to the observed error rate spike.

contributing_factors.description: Service auth in region eu-west experienced a configuration change.
why_chain: Service auth in region eu-west saw a change in error rate and request volume.
The change in error rate coincided with the introduction of the feature request.
The configuration change could have introduced a bug or unexpected behavior.

contributing_factors.description: Service auth in region eu-west saw a spike in p95 latency.
why_chain: Service auth in region eu-west had a spike in p95 latency.
The spike in latency could be due to the feature request or configuration change.
The spike in latency could also indicate a problem with the service itself.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a sudden increase in traffic.
ruled_out.reason: Request volume stayed about the same, contradicting this hypothesis.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a configuration change elsewhere in the system.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate spike was specific to service auth in region eu-west, not a system-wide issue.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service auth in region eu-west rose from 0.28% to 0.68% (+145%), with a change point at 2026-03-09T15:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth in region eu-west: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.26).
At the same time, request volume for service auth in region eu-west stayed about the same (391 per 5 min before, 439 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service auth in region eu-west stayed about the same (90 ms before, 91 ms after, +0%).
Feature request: dark mode for the account page. (catalog, eu-west; 287 min before the change; record R013)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 287 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Change records for the affected service/region
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Investigate the feature request R013 for any potential issues.
Review and test the configuration changes made to service auth in region eu-west.
Monitor the service auth in region eu-west for any further issues.
